comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## RCA — my framing of this ticket was WRONG. Problem 2 is intended behaviour; Problem 1 is real but did not cause it.

### Problem 2 — "the gate fails OPEN on a provider error" — REFUTED

The completion verifier **ran and PASSED**. The durable sidecar the close emitted proves it:

    .tickets-tracker/e369-a449-4773-48fb/1785827264280828001-...-COMPLETION_VERDICT.json
      verdict: PASS
      model:   bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
      criteria: 13 evaluated       findings: 0
      verified_at_sha: 996a3b107f8b78de78a497e6797741d5da42fac2

So verification was not skipped, not swallowed, and not degraded. The Bedrock haiku 400 came from a
DIFFERENT caller and was incidental to the close.

**Why no attestation, then.** `gate_ops.py:129` — `certifiable = not uncertified` — with the intent
stated verbatim above it:

> "Certification is WITHHELD iff a direct child is closed-but-UNCERTIFIED (force-closed): the parent
> MAY close (subject to its own criteria) but cannot be certified — certification propagates, so an
> unattested descendant withholds the parent's signature. **This is a close-vs-certify distinction,
> NOT a block.**"

`transition_close.py:409` then returns before signing. Close proceeds, exit 0, no attestation — by
design, and documented at the line.

**The two uncertified descendants, enumerated:**

    0059  bug  DC inbound filing is a no-op in live CI: reconcile r…
    2bc7  bug  Test helpers return an unregistered copy of mutation…

Both are `closed` with no `completion-verifier` attestation. All 39 other descendants carry one.

**Ruled out along the way, each with evidence:**
 * gate disabled → `gates.gate_enabled(...) = True` for the epic, identical to a bug that DID certify.
 * duplicate/not-a-bug skip → `_has_live_replacement_link(...) = False`.
 * type-based skip → the skip list is `("session_log","code_review","identity")`; `epic` is absent.
 * verify-vs-sign drift → `_material_drifted` needs the two SHAs to differ; `verified_at_sha` equals
   the close worktree's HEAD exactly, and the reflog shows HEAD last moved 06:51 UTC, before the
   close started at ~06:52 (error at 07:05).
 * recovery swallowing the error → `completion_recovery.py:553` re-raises `CompletionRecoveryError`.

**Classification: `intended-behavior`.** Authority: the cited design comment at `gate_ops.py:126-129`
plus the matching contract in `transition_close.py:405-410`. There is no defect to repair here, and
"fixing" it would break certification propagation — an epic could then be certified while part of
its subtree is not.

### Problem 1 — the Bedrock 400 — CONFIRMED as a real, separate defect

`review_kernel/verify.py:301 model_max_output_tokens` maps by substring (haiku 64K, sonnet/opus
128K) and `max_output_cfg` **only ever RAISES**:

    return cfg if cap <= cfg.max_tokens else replace(cfg, max_tokens=cap)

So a cap raised for a 128K model is carried into a later call that resolves to the 64K haiku and is
never re-clamped. Bedrock validates strictly and rejects. Demonstrated as a pure function:

    max_output_cfg(Cfg(sonnet, 16000))            -> max_tokens = 128000
    replace(that, model=haiku) -> max_output_cfg  -> max_tokens = 128000   (haiku ceiling 64000)
    PREDICTION IF TRUE 128000 / IF FALSE 64000    -> CONFIRMED

This violates the function's OWN stated contract — "Unknown/absent models fall back CONSERVATIVELY
… so an unmapped model never requests an output larger than its provider accepts" — which the
shrinking-model case defeats. Classification: `defect`. Direct Anthropic tolerated it; Bedrock does
not, which is why `d2ce` (default local dev to Bedrock) surfaced it.

### What this means for closing e369

The epic does not need a gate change. It needs its two uncertified descendants certified — reopen
0059 and 2bc7, move each back to `in_progress`, re-close through the gate — after which a re-close
of the epic will sign. That is the documented remedy, and it satisfies the operator's rule that a
close without completion verification is prohibited.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## A THIRD DEFECT, and it is the real fail-open — reproduced deterministically

Re-ran the verifier standalone against e369 with full capture. It reproduces every time:

    32x  WARNING llm call [epic-bug-screen] mode=single_turn
         model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 FAILED in 0.4s: 400
         'The maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 64000'
    ...
    {"verdict": "PASS", "findings": [], ... "model": "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"}
    exit=0

**Thirty-two failures, and a PASS.** The step is `epic_bug_screen.py:170 _row`:

    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — degrade open per candidate; the close never fails here
        logger.warning("epic bug screen call failed for %s; degrading to C (unrelated)", ...)
        verdict = dict(_DEGRADE)

`_DEGRADE` is verdict **C — 'unrelated'**, the most permissive outcome. So each bug that cannot be screened is silently declared unrelated to the epic.

### Why the three defects compose into something worse than any of them

 1. **Problem 1** (no re-clamp when the model shrinks) makes the haiku screen call fail — not sometimes, but **100% of the time**, deterministically.
 2. **Problem 3** converts each failure into 'unrelated'. Per-candidate degradation is a deliberate, defensible choice; it was never designed for the case where the failure is SYSTEMATIC.
 3. Result: the epic's caused_by bug floor — the check that asks 'did this epic's own work break something still open?' — **evaluated nothing at all**, and said so nowhere. Not in the verdict, not in the sidecar, not in the exit code.

That is a safety check that disappears exactly when its dependency is misconfigured, which is the same shape as the enrich-drain push failure earlier tonight: a subsystem reporting success while doing nothing.

**Note this is EPIC-SPECIFIC**, which explains the whole puzzle. `epic-bug-screen` runs only for epics, so the seven bug closes tonight never touched it and all certified normally. Only e369 hit it.

### Classification

`defect`, but the REMEDY is a design decision I am not making unilaterally. The per-candidate degrade is intentional and cited in the code. What is missing is an **aggregate** signal: when every candidate degrades (or some threshold does), the gate should either fail closed or record 'screen unavailable — N candidates unevaluated' on the verdict, so a reader can tell 'no related bugs found' from 'the screen never ran'. Options worth weighing: fail closed on total degradation; carry an `unevaluated` count into the verdict and sidecar; or keep degrading but refuse to CERTIFY when the screen was blind.

Recording rather than fixing, because changing when an epic close blocks is a gate-semantics change that deserves an explicit ruling.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## FINAL REPORT — rebar-debug protocol complete

**Problem.** The completion verifier 400'd on Bedrock, and an epic closed with no attestation.

**Proven root causes — three, each explaining distinct symptoms, none redundant.**

1. **The 400** — `review_kernel/verify.py:301` maps model→ceiling by substring, and
   `max_output_cfg` **only ever RAISES** (`return cfg if cap <= cfg.max_tokens else …`). A cap
   raised for the 128K verifier rides into a later call resolving to the 64K trivial model and is
   never re-clamped. Anthropic tolerated it; Bedrock rejects it.
2. **The blind gate** — `epic_bug_screen.py:170` degrades a failed screen to **C, "unrelated"**.
   Per-candidate that is deliberate and documented; when 32 of 32 fail it silently turns the
   caused_by bug floor into a no-op with no aggregate signal.
3. **The missing attestation** — `gate_ops.py:129` `certifiable = not uncertified`, documented at
   the line as "a close-vs-certify distinction, NOT a block". Two descendants (`0059`, `2bc7`) are
   closed-but-uncertified, so the signature was correctly withheld. **`intended-behavior`, not a
   defect — my original framing of this ticket was wrong.**

**Proof.** Cause 1 by pure function (predicted 128000-if-true / 64000-if-false → 128000), then
live. Causes 1+2 together by re-running the identical command with only the clamp differing:

    BEFORE  128 provider 400s, 32/32 screens FAILED  ->  verdict PASS
    AFTER     0 provider 400s,  0 screens failed     ->  verdict FAIL (exit 1)

Cause 3 by the durable sidecar (`verdict: PASS`, 13 criteria, `verified_at_sha` == HEAD) plus
direct branch tests, having ruled out: gate disabled, the duplicate/not-a-bug skip, a type-based
skip, verify-vs-sign drift (SHAs identical; reflog shows HEAD static), and recovery swallowing.

**Test.** `tests/unit/test_max_tokens_model_ceiling_1019.py` — seen RED first for the right reason
(`assert 128000 <= 64000`, after I corrected an earlier RED that failed on my own incomplete stub),
GREEN after, and returned to RED by re-introducing the exact root cause (mutation check), then
restored. Carries a positive control (a 128K model is untouched), a request-clamp-still-wins cell,
and unmapped-model cells.

**Fix.** Clamp the request to the resolved model's ceiling at `structured_run.build_model_settings`
— the point where the model is definitively known and the 400 originates. Applied **only** to a
model the table knows: `model_max_output_tokens` substitutes the configured default for an unmapped
model, and clamping to that would silently shrink a deliberate operator floor — a regression worse
than the bug. Gerrit 1361.

**Scope & safety.** Restores behaviour, adds no dependency, weakens no test. No caller depends on
sending an over-ceiling request — such a request cannot succeed, only 400. Unit suite **7851
passed, 24 skipped**.

**Siblings.** Construct sweep: `workflow/runs.py:180,192` use the same monotonic-raise
(`max(cfg.max_tokens, …)`) and are the *sources* of the inflated cap; they are caught at the wire
by this clamp rather than each needing its own. Parity sweep: `structured_run.py:297` is the ONLY
site writing `model_settings["max_tokens"]`; `runner.py:423` is its only caller and `agent_call.py`
merely receives the dict — so the choke point is structurally complete, not merely swept.

**Replication.** The original report no longer reproduces: zero 400s, zero screen failures, and the
verifier reaches a real verdict.

**Residual risk & prevention.**
 * **Cause 2 — ticket filed here, NOT fixed.** The remedy (fail closed on total degradation? carry
   an `unevaluated` count? refuse to CERTIFY when the screen was blind?) changes when an epic close
   blocks, which is a gate-semantics ruling for the operator, not a debug-session decision.
 * **`set_parent`'s non-sub-task branch has no read-back**, unlike the sub-task branch 1a9f fixed —
   accepted here, tracked on [rebar:4b9e-bcad-456a-4233].
 * **Two uncertified descendants** (`0059`, `2bc7`) — accepted; they are the documented reason the
   epic cannot be certified, and the remedy is to re-close them through the gate.

comments.body:
## OPERATOR-RATIFIED DECISION (2026-08-04): FAIL CLOSED

The operator has ruled on the open design question from the prior RCA (the third
defect — the epic-close bug screen converting a systematic provider failure into
per-candidate "unrelated" verdicts, silently blinding the caused_by bug floor):

**An LLM provider error during the completion verifier must BLOCK the close** —
nonzero exit, a clear error naming the provider failure, ticket stays
`in_progress` — consistent with the absent-provider path, which already fails
closed. The escape hatch is the existing force flag (`--force-close` today;
story 24f7-1955-bcd8-4f29 separately renames it to `--force` — the rename is NOT
part of this change).

Concretely for this ticket: `LLMUnavailableError` raised anywhere inside the
completion-verifier run — including from the epic-close bug screen's
per-candidate calls — must propagate to the close gate's existing fail-closed
handler instead of degrading to a `C` ("unrelated") verdict. Non-provider
per-candidate failures (malformed output, store read glitches) keep the
documented degrade-open behavior: only the SYSTEMIC provider-error class fails
closed.

Implementation proceeds under this ticket per the plan now recorded in the
description.

compiled_state.description:
# The completion-verifier close gate FAILS OPEN on an LLM provider error (via the epic-close bug screen)

## Context / Problem

Closing epic `e369-a449-4773-48fb`, the completion verifier's epic-close bug
screen hit a Bedrock `ValidationException` (`LLMUnavailableError`) on every one
of its 32 per-candidate calls — and the verifier still returned PASS, exit 0.
The screen's `except Exception` degrade coerces EVERY per-candidate failure to
verdict `C` ("unrelated"), so a systematic provider outage silently turns the
epic's caused_by bug floor into a no-op with no signal anywhere: not in the
verdict, not in the sidecar, not in the exit code. Contrast: when the provider
package is merely absent, the same gate correctly REFUSES the close. Two
failure modes of one dependency, opposite outcomes — and the fail-open one
fires exactly when the provider is degraded. (Full RCA in the comments; the
original "the outer gate swallows the error" framing was refuted — the outer
close gate already fails closed on any exception from `verify_completion`. The
real fail-open is the screen-layer degrade.)

The prior RCA's other confirmed defect — `max_tokens` never re-clamped for a
smaller model, the source of the 400 itself — is already fixed and merged
(commit `e49e7a418a`, Gerrit change 1361).

**Operator-ratified decision (2026-08-04, recorded in the comments): FAIL
CLOSED.** A provider error during the completion verifier must BLOCK the close
(nonzero exit, error naming the provider failure, ticket stays `in_progress`),
consistent with the absent-provider path. The escape hatch is the existing
force flag (`--force-close`; its rename to `--force` is story
24f7-1955-bcd8-4f29, out of scope here).

## Approach

Make the epic-close bug screen propagate `LLMUnavailableError` instead of
degrading it to `C`, at both layers where it is currently swallowed:

1. `epic_bug_screen.screen_candidates._row` — re-raise `LLMUnavailableError`
   before the broad per-candidate degrade (warm call and fan-out alike; the
   `ThreadPoolExecutor.map` surfaces the first worker exception on iteration).
2. `epic_bug_screen.run_screen` — re-raise `LLMUnavailableError` before the
   outer "the screen is advisory" broad except.

**The exact re-raise predicate at both seams is `except LLMUnavailableError:
raise` — the ordinary isinstance catch, which by design also covers its
subclass `LLMConfigError` (`errors.py`: `class
LLMConfigError(LLMUnavailableError)`).** That is intended, not accidental:
both the systemic-outage class (the Bedrock 400) and the absent-provider /
missing-extra class fail closed, matching the posture the pinned
`test_gate_missing_llm_fails_closed` already asserts at the outer gate seam.
Worked example: a screen call raising
`LLMUnavailableError("the LLM provider call failed: … ValidationException")`
propagates and blocks the close; a screen call raising `RuntimeError("model
exploded")` or producing malformed output still degrades that candidate to
`C`. Do NOT narrow with `type(exc) is LLMUnavailableError`. Non-systemic
failures (malformed output, store read errors, any non-`LLMUnavailableError`
exception) keep the documented degrade-open behavior.

Why the FAN-OUT re-raises too, diverging from the `plan_review/pass1.py`
container precedent (which aborts only the warm call and degrades a fanned-out
worker's systemic error): pass1's fan-out can degrade because the earlier
Pass-1 chunk pool re-raises `LLMUnavailableError` before the container stage is
ever reached — an upstream tripwire owns the outage signal. The completion
screen has NO such upstream tripwire: `produce_completion_verdict` preflights
once, but a per-call provider rejection (the motivating 32/32 Bedrock
`ValidationException`) is invisible to that single preflight, so the screen's
own fan-out is the ONLY place the outage can surface. The alternative
(warm-call-only abort) was weighed and rejected — it restores fail-open for
exactly the systematic-failure scenario this ticket exists to close. From there the existing machinery already
does the right thing with no further change: the workflow interpreter captures
the step exception as a failed step, `produce_completion_verdict` raises on a
non-succeeded run, and `transition_close._completion_precheck`'s fail-closed
handler blocks the close with the standard "completion verification could not
run (…) Override with --force-close" message carrying the provider failure
text. `--force-close` bypasses the verifier before the screen ever runs, so the
escape hatch is untouched. Docstrings/comments that state "the screen never
blocks a close" are updated to name the one deliberate exception. This does not
regress Gerrit change 1360 (`_legacy_material_ok` grandfathering, the
certifiable=False stderr warning, `certifiable` in the PASS sidecar): none of
those paths are touched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py` — the two re-raise seams + docstrings.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py` — comment/docstring accuracy only.
- `tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py` and/or a new
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_provider_error_1019.py` — the RED-first
  behavioral tests below.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py` — a provider-error
  close-refusal case at the gate seam if not already covered.

## Testing

RED first (each fails on current main, for the right reason):

- a screen call raising `LLMUnavailableError` propagates out of
  `screen_candidates` (warm-call and fan-out cases) and out of `run_screen` —
  driving the seam to RAISE, not asserting a mock's call count;
- end-to-end at the close-gate seam: a verifier run that dies with a provider
  error blocks the close — nonzero exit, ticket stays `in_progress`, no
  signature, the error message names the provider failure.

Pinned-unchanged (must stay green):

- non-provider per-candidate failures still degrade to `C`
  (`test_screen_per_candidate_failure_degrades_to_c`,
  `test_run_screen_degrades_open_on_total_failure`);
- absent-provider/missing-extra close still fails closed
  (`test_gate_missing_llm_fails_closed`);
- `--force-close` still bypasses (`test_force_close_skips_verify_and_sign`);
- healthy PASS close still mints the signed attestation per change-1360
  behavior (`test_gate_pass_closes_and_signs_after_close`,
  `test_gate_pass_uncertifiable_warns_on_stderr`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a completion-verifier run in which the epic-close bug screen raises
      `LLMUnavailableError` REFUSES the close: nonzero exit, ticket stays
      `in_progress`, no signature, the error names the provider failure, and
      the existing `--force-close` escape hatch still applies — checked by the
      new gate-seam test passing.
- [ ] a test pins the refusal by driving the screen to RAISE the provider
      error (not by asserting on a mock's call count) — checked by the new
      unit tests in the screen module's suite passing, RED-first.
- [ ] non-provider screen failures still degrade open, and the absent-provider,
      force-close, and healthy-PASS close paths are byte-for-byte unchanged —
      checked by the pre-existing tests named in ## Testing staying green.
- [ ] the `max_tokens` re-clamp for a smaller model (the source of the original
      400) is merged — checked by commit `e49e7a418a` reachable from `main`.
- [ ] epic e369's close disposition is explicitly recorded on this ticket:
      either re-verified once the gate works, or its unsigned close accepted
      with the reason stated — checked by a closing comment on this ticket.
